Trail Conditions

     
    • Wilderness Backpacking Permits are required for all overnight hikes, year-round.
      • For the most up to date information on how to obtain a permit, visit our Wilderness Trip Planner page.
    • All food, garbage, beverages & scented items must be stored in park-approved bear canisters.
    • Note about human waste resource impacts: In the last few years there has been a rise in human feces left unburied within the park and wilderness. In order to keep this a pristine and enjoyable resource into the future:
      • Always use toilets when available
      • When beyond 1/4 mile of a privy - walk at least 70 steps (200 feet) away from water, trails, and campsites, & dig a hole 8 inches deep in soil (not sand) to bury your human waste. Pack out your toilet paper.
    • For more updates, always check weather & road conditions.
    • Olympic National Forest alerts and conditions page
    • Visit our Interactive Wilderness Trip Planner Map to see an overview of campsite locations
     

    These conditions are updated as reported from visitors and staff and may not reflect the what you find in the field. Conditions can change quickly in this wilderness park.

     

    Coastal Trail Conditions

     

    Northside Trail Conditions

     

    • Due to a road washout, the Elwha area is closed to vehicle access beyond the Madison Falls parking area. This adds an additional 6.5 miles of hiking to the Whiskey Bend Trailhead and ~8 miles to the Boulder Creek Trailhead.

    • The Elwha River and its tributaries are closed to fishing

    Elwha River Trail Whiskey Bend to Lake Margaret 27.7 miles
    1198' to 3650'
    • Trail has been cleared of downed trees to Hayes River Camp
    • 45 trees down between Hayes River and Chicago Camp. This section of trail has several sections of very brushy trail as well
    • Visitors are reminded that there are still fire damaged areas of the trail between Hayes River Camp and Chicago Camp and to be alert for the following hazards: falling trees and branches, trail damage, loose rocks, and windblown dust and ash.
    • Creek crossings may be difficult or impossible, particularly in the winter through the early summer or during periods of high rainfall.  The river crossing south of Chicago Camp has been reported as no longer having a downed tree across it and needs to be forded.
    • The stretch of trail between Low Divide Camp and Chicago Camp has been reported as being overgrown and difficult to follow in some sections. 
    • ~0.5 miles south of Hayes River jct. a 20' section of trail is being undercut by a landslide - proceed with caution.
    		 8/23/26
    Humes Ranch Loop Geyser Valley, Krause Bottom, Rica Canyon & Humes Ranch Loop 4.3 miles

    • Trail has been cleared of downed trees.

    Boulder Creek Trail Olympic Hot Springs and Appleton Pass via Boulder Creek Trailhead 1800' to 5100'  
    • A year-round burn ban is in effect for the Boulder Creek Campground / Olympic Hot Springs area.
    • Reports of potential habituated bear around the Boulder Creek camp area.  Visitors should always practice good food storage while in the Wilderness. 
    • There are several large trees across the road but the route is accessible to all. Bikers will have to dismount to cross a few of the downed trees on the road to the trailhead. 
      • Bikes are not allowed beyond the Boulder Creek Trailhead and visitors must walk the remaining 2.4 miles to the hot springs.     
    		 06/14/26

    Southside Trail Conditions

     

    • Due to a washout on South Shore Road, the only access to Graves Creek and North Fork Quinault trailheads is via North Shore Road
    • The Quinault Wilderness Information Center, located at 913 North Shore Road, is closed for the 2026 season. See our Wilderness Center Page for more information. 
    • Bear canisters are required for all overnightwilderness camping
    Trail Name Description Mileage & Elevation Conditions Last Updated

    Skyline Primitive Trail Elip Creek Trail via Kimta Peak to North Fork Quinault Trail 20.1 miles
    3350' to 5400'    		  
    • Expect to encounter brushy, overgrown sections of trail and areas of very narrow trail tread, espcially between Kimta Peak and Lake Beauty. Hikers should expect to travel much slower through this section due to route finding and areas of very narrow or non existent trail tread. Budgeting more time for travel through this section is highly recommended
    • Expect to encounter washed out sections of trail in several gullies between Seattle Creek and Kimta Peak
    • Due to the primitive/unmaintained nature of this trail, expect to encounter downed trees and several brushy sections of trail.
    • Expert route finding/navigational skills recommended. This route is strenuous with frequent elevation gain & loss.
    • No water sources between Kimta Peak and Three Prune
    • Closed to stock
    		 9/29/26

    North Fork Quinault River Trail Trailhead to Lake Margaret 16.5 miles
    515’ to 3635’    		  
    • The fords at Wild Rose Creek, Elip Creek & the Quinault River south of Sixteen Mile camp may become impassable during heavy precipitation & snowmelt
    • A tree fell onto the Stalding Creek bridge and resulted in structural damage to the bridge and some of the planks. The bridge is considered closed at this time. Visitors can see if the creek below is fordable as a possible alternative to cross, though, it may be too swift to cross in the winter months and into the early summer, or during periods of heavy rain/snowmelt.   
    • Trail snowfee through Low Divide
    • Trail has been cleared of downed trees to Low Divide
    		 9/29/26
    East Fork Quinault River Trail Trailhead to Anderson Pass 18.2 miles
    646' to 4465'    		  
    • South Shore road is closed due to a washout outside the park boundary. The only access to Graves Creek trailhead is via North Shore road
    • There is a washed out section of trail 1/3 prior to reaching the Enchanted Valley chalet/campsites. Hikers should be prepared to either ford the river or route find up a steep hillside to reach Enchanted Valley
    • Trail has been cleared of downed trees to Enchanted Valley
    • White Creek, below the O'Neil Pass Jct., must be forded, and can be swift/deep during periods of heavy rainfall or times of heavy snow-melt in the high country.  These conditions typically occur through the fall/winter and continue into the early summer.  Expect the possibility of not being able to ford if traveling during these times.    
    • All food and scented items must be stored in bear canisters
    • Enchanted Valley has a large population of bears; stay a minimum of 50 yards away from park wildlife.
    • **The Hart Lake and Lacrosse Lake Cutoff Routes may appear on some GPS devices/maps, but these are not trails. Hikers attempting these routes should expect cross-country conditions with steep/brushy slopes, loose rocks and no signage**
    		 9/29/26
    Six Ridge Primative Route Graves Creek Trailhead to Lake Sundown 7.3 miles
    605' to 3836'

    Gross Elevation Gain: 3,918'    		  
    • Trail closed as of 8/1/25 due to Bear Gulch Fire
    • Expect to encounter snow and challenging route finding conditions along this route during the winter and into early summer on a typical year. Ice axe recommended due to the number of steep, exposed slopes traversed on route, especially near Lake Sundown/Sundown Pass
    • This route is primitive and unmaintained with very brushy and rocky trail sections, particularly between Success Creek - Lake Sundown.  Between Six Ridge Pass - Belview has repeated gains and losses of elevation and route finding challenges. 
    		 9/29/26
